messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 latency spike detected on /v1/stream (streaming-route-a). SLOs breached (p95 120ms -> 340ms, p99 520ms -> 1.8s). Rolling 5m window. auto-notify:oncall.
Maya: acked. I'm oncall. seeing lots of streaming stall traces and increased tail for paging requests.
Joel: confirmed in dashboards — spike started ~2142507830. Error rates low, but token stream stalls and delayed first-chunk.
Rachel: any deploys around that time? I see a prefix-hash rollout finished ~2142507600 (prefixhash v2.3.0) — could be related.
Sanjay: check KV cache hit rate for streaming prefixes. I see hit-rate dropped from ~86% to 28% for prefix namespace stream-pref-1.
Eli: dumping recent cache eviction log for that shard:
```
2026-03-15T18:04:25Z shard-17 evict keyprefix=abc123.. ttl=5s reason=rollout
2026-03-15T18:05:12Z shard-17 miss keyprefix=abc123.. count=47
2026-03-15T18:06:03Z shard-17 miss keyprefix=abc123.. count=92
```
Carla: interesting — rollout triggered a prefix-key format change, we suspected compatibility but thought we had a safe migration.
Maya: immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback prefix-hash deploy 2) extend cache TTLs to warm 3) route streaming-route-a to fallback model variant (stateless) to avoid heavy KV lookups.
Joel: can we do TTL bump quickly? ops-runner suggests a config toggle for the cache-acceptor to set default_ttl from 5s -> 60s per shard. That should restore hit rate fast.
Sanjay: TTL change: issuing patch to cache-config in prod: `kubectl -n runtime set configmap cache-acceptor --from-literal=default_ttl=60` — applying to shard pool-1.
Maya: go ahead. Also start owner contact: @eng-runtime/lead for prefix migration rollback plan.
Eli: TTL patch applied to pool-1 at 2142508082. Patch diff: `default_ttl: 5 -> 60`
Rachel: after TTL bump: observing hit-rate recover from 28% -> 72% within 30s. p95 down from 340ms -> 150ms. p99 still high ~700ms though.
Joel: p99 tail still elevated due to cold KV misses and ongoing background compaction. Let's also enable temporary traffic reroute: send 20% of streaming-route-a to fallback-route (no prefix lookup).
Maya: initiating canary reroute via routing service: `POST /admin/routes/rebalance {route: streaming-route-a, fallback: streaming-fallback, percent: 20}`. Doing now.
Carla: can we also pause the prefix-hash rollout? I see the rollout controller still finishing batches.
Sanjay: paused rollout at 2142508200. controller: `rollout/prefixhash-v2.3.0 paused by ops`
Eli: logs show older clients still emitting old-format keys; the new hash changed canonicalization so they miss current entries. Pausing prevents making it worse.
Rachel: with TTL bump + 20% reroute + rollout paused, p95 stabilizing ~130ms, p99 trending down to ~420ms. Streaming stalls reduced.
Maya: customer impact: investigated top five tenants affected — three experienced elevated latency for streaming sessions (not complete failures). CS pager notified for accounts A-238, B-991; no error escalations yet.
Carla: open action: investigate migration compat tests failure — seems we missed a client lib edge-case. Assigning to @eng-runtime + @client-libs.
Joel: follow-up runbook steps: 1) keep TTL=60 for 1 hour 2) let hit-rate stabilize 3) collect top prefixes with high churn 4) decide rollback vs. reconcile mapping tool to backfill keys.
Maya: handing off to next oncall (Carla) at 2142508400. Notes: TTL bumped, rollout paused, 20% reroute, hit-rate recovering. Watch p99 for the next 30m.
oncall-bot: HANDOFF: Next oncall: Carla. Link: https://redwood.internal/oncall/2142507890.
Carla: acked handoff. I'll take 2hr watch window. Creating follow-up ticket with logs and suggested action items.
Sanjay: ticket created: RW-INC-2142507890, includes KV dump, rollout changelog, TTL patch diff.
Eli: logs captured for forensic: s3://redwood-incident-logs/2142507890/ (compressed).
Rachel: postmortem checklist: capture root cause (prefix-hash compatibility), mitigation timeline, customer impact summary, and test gaps in client-libs. Assign owners in doc.
Maya: closing live mitigation — moving to monitoring phase. If p99 resurges, escalate to all-hands.
Carla: thanks team. leaving notes for CS + SOC. I'll follow up with a rollback decision if backfill isn't feasible in 3 hours. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED (mitigated): state=mitigated, severity=sev2, mitigations=ttl_bump,route_reroute,rollout_pause.
